# Wooden crate packing manual

The crate identifier follows the shell for its lifetime. The contents label identifies the shipment, so replace a contents label without erasing the shell identifier. These instructions describe packaging arrangements, not acceptance of the packed ceramic item.

## Empty shell check
Record the shell identifier and whether the interior is empty. Set aside a shell with a missing divider or unreadable shell mark. A previous shipment label must be removed before new contents labels are attached, while the permanent shell identifier stays legible.

## Stacked production tiles
Place a separator between every two production tiles and orient the stack against the rectangular pad. Keep the stack identifier visible from the lid side. A stack pattern does not fit an oblong demonstration specimen merely because the same shell can contain it.

## Oblong samples
For one oblong demonstration sample in a wooden crate, fit two crescent supports under its marked bearing points, wrap the body once in the plain sleeve, and leave the ends free of compression. Secure the supports to the crate's base slots and place a diagram of their locations inside the lid. Gently check for free movement before closing; any movement requires refitting the supports. Do not stack another piece above this sample.

This arrangement is complete for a local oblong-sample shipment. The carton guide is for rectangular paperboard sample packs and does not add an insert or a stacking rule to this arrangement.

## Divider storage
Store removed dividers by stamped shape code. A divider whose stamp cannot be read goes to the repair tray. Shape resemblance is insufficient because two divider families differ at the hidden seating tabs.

## Lid and closure record
Keep the lid paired to its shell and record the closure station. If a shell is reopened, retain the earlier closure entry and add the reopening observation. A closure entry is a packaging event, not proof of product conformity.

## Unpacking observation
At receiving, retain an observed damaged divider with the shell until the packaging assessment is recorded. Separate transport damage from bench observations made before dispatch. The run lineage remains attached to the product even when its shell is changed.
